cards.label: M8 base mounting bolt
cards.q: What holds the UR5e base down, and how tight?
cards.a: Four M8 bolts, strength class 8.8, at 20 N·m, seated in Ø13.5 mm counterbores on a Ø132 mm circle.

cards.label: Ø8 locating pin (optional)
cards.q: How can a UR5e go back on its mount in exactly the same place?
cards.a: Pins in the base's two Ø8 F8 holes (+0.030/+0.008 mm) locate it. Where those holes sit is estimated here.

cards.label: Joint housing (aluminium)
cards.q: Which UR5e joints are size 3, and which are size 1?
cards.a: Size 3: J0–J2, the base, shoulder and elbow, rated 150 N·m. Size 1: the three wrists J3–J5, rated 28 N·m.

cards.label: Black flexible flat-ring (covers joint connection)
cards.q: Why is the black flat-ring replaced every time a UR joint is reassembled?
cards.a: It covers the joint connection, and a fresh ring is what keeps the arm's IP rating.

cards.label: Half-clamp (bracket connection)
cards.q: How do you tighten a UR5e joint clamp?
cards.a: One side to a 1.0–1.5 mm gap, the other side to 4.0 N·m, then the first side to 4.0 N·m; both gaps must match.

cards.label: M5 socket head cap screw (clamp)
cards.q: What tool and torque close the UR5e clamp connections, base through elbow?
cards.a: A 4 mm hex key at 4.0 N·m. That key size drives an ISO 4762 M5 cap screw, so M5 is shown.

cards.label: Blue lid
cards.q: What is the first step in servicing any UR joint?
cards.a: Undo the screws in the blue lid and lift it off; that exposes the joint PCB's power and communication terminals.

cards.label: Main output bearing
cards.q: Which bearing types does UR's joint patent name at the output?
cards.a: Main bearings seated on inclined housing surfaces, with a crossed-roller or a four-point-contact bearing as alternatives.

cards.label: Circular spline (strain-wave gear)
cards.q: Why does a strain-wave gear reach a high ratio in a single stage?
cards.a: The flexspline has two fewer teeth than the rigid circular spline, so each motor turn moves the output on by only two teeth.

cards.label: Flexspline cup (strain-wave gear)
cards.q: What does the flexspline do in a UR joint's gear?
cards.a: This thin steel cup has teeth on its rim; the elliptical wave generator bends it into the circular spline at two opposite points.

cards.label: Wave generator (elliptical cam + flexible bearing)
cards.q: What is the high-speed input of a strain-wave gear?
cards.a: The wave generator: an elliptical cam on the motor axle, ringed by a thin flexible ball bearing.

cards.label: Motor stator (laminations)
cards.q: Why is a motor stator stacked from thin laminations?
cards.a: Thin insulated steel sheets block the eddy currents a solid core would carry, cutting heat and loss.
cards.root: stator ← Latin stāre, 'to stand': the part that stays still

cards.label: Stator windings (copper)
cards.q: What do the copper windings on the stator do?
cards.a: They carry the phase currents that build a rotating magnetic field; the rotor's magnets follow it round.
cards.root: copper ← Latin cuprum, from aes Cyprium, 'metal of Cyprus'

cards.label: Rotor with permanent magnets on hollow motor axle
cards.q: Why is a UR joint's motor axle hollow?
cards.a: So cables from the neighbouring joints can run straight through the joint's centre (UR patent US8410732B2).

cards.label: Friction ring
cards.q: Where does a UR joint brake make its friction?
cards.a: Between annular friction members and the brake member on the motor axle, so a locked brake can still slip.

cards.label: Brake member with six protrusions
cards.q: Why can you force a braked UR joint to move?
cards.a: The brake is a friction clutch: the pin blocks one of six protrusions, and very high torque makes it slip instead of break.

cards.label: Wave spring (brake preload)
cards.q: What sets the slip torque of a UR joint brake?
cards.a: A wave spring presses the brake member between two locking members; moving one locking member changes the preload.
cards.root: sine ← Latin sinus, from Arabic jayb (جيب), 'fold, pocket'

cards.label: Brake solenoid
cards.q: What engages a UR joint brake when power drops?
cards.a: A small solenoid on the joint PCB drives a pin into the annular brake member.

cards.label: Brake pin / ratchet
cards.q: What physically stops a UR joint motor when its brake engages?
cards.a: A pin, pushed by the solenoid, catches one protrusion of the brake member on the motor axle.

cards.label: Motor-side encoder disc
cards.q: Where does a UR joint measure its motor angle?
cards.a: From a disc on the motor axle, read by encoder 133 on the back of the joint PCB (patent US8410732B2).

cards.label: Joint PCB (motor drive, encoders, brake)
cards.q: What does a single UR joint PCB carry?
cards.a: The motor drive, the output encoder on its front, the motor encoder on its back and the brake solenoid; an aluminium plate sinks its heat.

cards.label: PCB components
cards.q: Are the small blocks on each UR joint PCB the real component layout?
cards.a: No. They're representative: UR doesn't publish its board layout.

cards.label: Output-side encoder disc (on hollow output axle)
cards.q: Why does a UR joint also measure its angle after the gear?
cards.a: Gear backlash and flex would hide the true angle; a second encoder on the output axle reads the joint directly.

cards.label: Aluminium tube
cards.q: How far apart are the UR5e joint axes along the upper arm and the forearm?
cards.a: 425 mm along the upper arm and 392.2 mm along the forearm. The upper arm is the heaviest link, 8.058 kg.

cards.label: M3 countersunk Torx screw (a)
cards.q: Separating a UR wrist joint: which screws come out first, and what torque do they go back at?
cards.a: The countersunk M3 Torx TX10 screws (a), refitted at 0.9 N·m; then the rest (b). Support the joint, it can drop.

cards.label: M3 cylinder-head Torx screw (b)
cards.q: What torque do the cylinder-head M3 screws in UR wrist joints take?
cards.a: 1.3 N·m with a Torx TX10. Before refitting, clean each threaded hole with an M3 tap, as the manual says.

cards.label: Teflon ring
cards.q: What sits under the black flat-ring at a UR wrist connection?
cards.a: A Teflon ring. It comes off right after the flat-ring when the joint is separated.

cards.label: Tool output flange (EN ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6)
cards.q: Decode the UR5e flange standard EN ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6.
cards.a: Ø50 mm bolt circle, 4 holes, M6 thread. It adds a Ø31.5 centring bore and a Ø6 pin hole; tool screws are class 8.8 at 8 N·m.
cards.terms: EN: European Norm · ISO: International Organization for Standardization
